problem: End-to-end learned navigation policies are almost only evaluated in simulation; real-robot evaluations are rare, done in simplified lab conditions, and give little insight into generalization or what the agent's visual reasoning actually does.
motivation: Real-robot navigation experiments are costly and hard to reproduce, so it is unclear whether sim-trained PointGoal agents transfer without sim2real adaptation, how they use RGB-D versus GPS, and whether noisy simulation can stand in for real tests. The authors deploy agents on two real buildings, a furnished castle and an office space, that have challenging conditions such as glass, mirrors, carpets and slippery floors.
key_idea: Pre-train a Habitat ResNet+GRU PPO PointGoal agent on many simulated scenes (Gibson), fine-tune it on a 3D scan of the target building, and deploy it directly to a LoCoBot with no sim2real technique, then analyze sensor usage with Grad-CAM and compare real results with noisy simulation.
insight: Pre-training on many scenes followed by fine-tuning on the scanned target scene gives the smallest sim2real gap (INSAL real: SR 100 / SPL 92.2 vs Targeted 80.0 / 47.1 and Gibson-only 50.0 / 31.7), while training only on the target scene generalizes poorly to unseen regions (NLE real unseen SR 33.3). Grad-CAM shows the agent relies on depth only when needed (blocking obstacles, turning points), while GPS importance stays flat. In the noisy-sim study, visual sensor noise barely matters, but actuator noise reproduces or exceeds the real-world performance drop, so it is the noise type that makes a useful proxy.
method: Agent: Habitat baseline policy with a ResNet visual encoder, a GRU memory and a noisy GPS vector plus previous action as inputs, trained with PPO; 160x120 RGB-D matched to the LoCoBot RealSense camera.

Sim-to-real deployment: discrete actions (forward, left, right, stop) are executed by the ROS move_base stack; AMCL gives localization and the GPS vector, and the map exported from Habitat shares the coordinate system so the same episodes run in sim and real.

Agent variants: Gibson (trained on 72 Gibson scenes, 3.6M episodes, unseen-environment case), Targeted (trained only on 50k episodes from the seen region of the scanned scene) and Finetuned (Gibson pre-training then fine-tuning on the scanned scene).

Environments and evaluation: Matterport-scanned NLE (castle, 11 eval episodes) and INSAL (offices, 10 eval episodes), with held-out 'unseen' regions; metrics SR, SPL and soft SPL; a habitat-lab interface wraps the real robot as a 'simulator'.

Interpretability: Grad-CAM on the last conv layer of the RGB-D encoder, using the gradient of the chosen action, plus accumulated visual-input importance over time, on obstacle, L-shaped path and per-action episodes.

Noisy-sim study: the Targeted agent is run on NLE with RGB noises (Gaussian, speckle, salt&pepper, Poisson), Redwood depth noise and actuator noise (P, MoveBase DWA, iLQR controllers, Habitat 2021 challenge noise) and compared with real, plus actuator error measurements.
Classical baseline: the ROS navigation stack with the exported map, evaluated with the same metrics.

setting.backbone: ResNet + GRU actor-critic policy (Habitat PointNav baseline), trained with PPO from scratch
setting.training_data: Gibson (72 scenes, 3.6M episodes) for pre-training; 50,000 episodes per target scene (NLE, INSAL) from Matterport scans for Targeted / fine-tuning
setting.observation: 160x120 RGB-D plus noisy GPS vector (distance and direction from ROS AMCL) and previous action
setting.action_space: discrete MOVE_FORWARD / TURN_LEFT / TURN_RIGHT / STOP, translated to continuous control by ROS move_base
setting.simulator: Habitat (training); real LoCoBot deployment in two buildings
setting.privileged: none for the learned agent beyond the GPS goal vector from localization on a pre-built map; the ROS baseline was given the full map

numbers.eval_set_note: 11 real-robot evaluation episodes in the NLE castle (seen + unseen regions)

numbers_note: Only small custom real-robot evaluation sets (10-11 episodes per scene) with no standard benchmark; the noisy-sim comparison is only in a figure, so no numbers were extracted. The ROS classical baseline (NLE overall SR 100 / SPL 84.3 / sSPL 83.0; INSAL 100 / 92.8 / 90.4) is not the paper's own method and is excluded.
results: The Finetuned agent reaches real-robot SR 90.9 / SPL 79.7 on NLE and SR 100 / SPL 92.2 on INSAL with no sim2real adaptation, with a small sim-real gap. It is slightly below the ROS classical planner (NLE SPL 84.3, INSAL 92.8, and the ROS agent had the full map) but comparable, and it beats the Targeted-only agent on both scenes. The Gibson-only agent transfers well on NLE but poorly on INSAL (SR 50.0).
limitations: Very small evaluation sets (10-11 episodes per scene) and only PointGoal with a localization-derived GPS, so the statistical power is low.
Grad-CAM analysis is qualitative, based on a few hand-picked episodes; the noisy-sim comparison is only reported in figures.
The best agents need a 3D scan of the target building and fine-tuning, and the unseen-environment case is not reliable (Gibson agent on INSAL).
